answer: Because the custody account is separate, someone cannot recycle one pool of capital across 108 aliases, and each one needs its own funded sparrow account. Deposits are visible in plume, and voyage reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 45% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Each duplicate costs another 82 dollars in locked collateral and another 9 days of waiting. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
